title: When a Small Fine-Tune's Margin Sits Inside Its Training-Seed Spread: Variance Decomposition, Class Memorization, and Prompt Confounds in Financial Reconciliation
description: Small fine-tuned language models are frequently reported to beat frontier models on narrow structured tasks from a single training run and a task-resampling confidence interval. We audit one such previously published claim---a 1.7B-parameter LoRA fine-tune outperforming DeepSeek v4-flash on severity-weighted recall (R_w) across 800 synthetic financial reconciliation tasks (0.9007 against 0.8719, margin 0.0288)---against a pre-registered seed-spread rule and five independent diagnostics. First, across four runs of one recipe on a 300-task development pool, R_w spans 0.7457 to 0.9451 (SD 0.0823, 2.86 times the margin), with the shipped run at the top; across the three unselected runs trained afterwards, SD is 0.0479 (1.66 times the margin, whose 95% chi-square interval includes the margin) and the shipped run sits 0.1448 above their mean. Accordingly, the single-run headline is retracted: the comparison is underpowered rather than reversed. Second, a nine-class decomposition shows that one class (\texttt{PARTIAL\_MATCH}, 32 tasks built from 9 abbreviation pairs that all appear in training) accounts for 112% of the margin; excluding it eliminates the lead (-0.0036, 95% CI [-0.0178, +0.0105]). Third, an exploratory rerun matching both models on a defined-class prompt and five-sample voting reverses the margin to -0.0288 (the fine-tune fails two of five guards), and comparing each model on its own best prompt still leaves DeepSeek ahead by 0.0701 (-0.0524 without \texttt{PARTIAL\_MATCH}). Fourth, the zero-shot base model (0.6002) scores below a constant-flagging floor (0.6673), and validation loss decouples from R_w across 14 checkpoints ($\rho = $ -0.608, spread 0.259). Reading a fine-tuning margin against training-seed variance, per-class contributions, trivial floors, and matched comparator budgets catches each failure cheaply; resolving a margin of 0.0288 requires tens of training runs on an untouched test pool rather than three. Not peer reviewed. Code, data and artifacts: https://github.com/caiotheodoro/reconforge
